title: DBR-Backed Chromium Absorber
scientific_hypothesis: A distributed Bragg reflector of HfO2/SiO2 pairs beneath a thin Cr layer will reflect near-infrared light back through the Cr for secondary absorption while the Cr at the air interface absorbs visible light directly, achieving high visible absorptance with high IR reflectance.
design_principle: DBR structures create high reflectivity bands through constructive interference of reflections from alternating high/low index layers. Placing Cr at the air interface captures visible light on first pass, while the DBR reflects IR and any transmitted visible back through Cr for additional absorption opportunities.
proposed_topology: Air / Cr / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / Al substrate
design_variables: HfO2 layer thickness in each pair (nm)
SiO2 layer thickness in each pair (nm)
soft_objectives: Minimize total layer count while meeting performance targets
manufacturing_considerations: Total 18 layers including Cr and 8 DBR pairs
Cr thickness must be controllable via sputtering
HfO2/SiO2 pairs require precise thickness control for DBR performance
L05 suggests stress management considerations for multilayer stacks
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
known_risks: Cr may absorb some IR reducing reflectance
DBR band edge may not align perfectly with 700 nm cutoff
Visible absorption may be limited by single Cr pass
execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer stack with air incidence on an aluminum substrate. Stack sequence from air to substrate: one chromium layer, followed by eight alternating pairs of HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) (HfO2 first in each pair), terminating at the aluminum substrate. Total layer count is 18 (1 Cr (Rakic-LD) + 16 dielectric + Al (Rakic-LD) substrate not counted as film layer). Optimize the thickness of the chromium layer and the thickness of each HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layer independently. Wavelength range 400-2000 nm. Target: maximize absorptance in 400-700 nm, maximize reflectance in 700-2000 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light.
